text:
mike: quick callout — our int8/4-bit runs on A100 are all over the place today. some kernels show ~1.8x speedup, others are slower than fp16. anyone seen this? :confused:
anya: yep saw that on the nightly canary. suspects: warmup pattern + kv cache miss behavior. runs that skip a proper prefix warmup end up doing more allocs and slow kernels.
dez: also kernel selector triggers different code paths based on seq len distribution. if batching mixes 1-token and 512-token requests we sometimes fall back to safer kernels.
rachel: FYI perf-bot picked up a regression on 2026-03-15 03:12 UTC: int8 avg tokens/sec -12% vs baseline for model=redwood-3-small@v2. linked flamegraph: https://perf.example/s/abc123 :eyes:
mike: can we agree a strict bench protocol for quantized comparisons? otherwise results aren't comparable between teams. proposing steps below.
anya: list them — short actionable so infra can script.
mike: protocol proposal:
- model/version: pin exact commit (no autoupdate)
- tokenizer: same sentencepiece/bpe files and detokenize config
- warmup: run 200 tokens of synthetic and 200 tokens of real prompt sequences before measurement
- kv state: run both cold and hot cache experiments; report both. cold=clear kv before each sample, hot=single long stream
- batching: keep batch shape distribution fixed; provide hist file that our bench harness reads
- power: run at default, 250W, and 200W. report power telemetry.
- seeds: set deterministic rng where applicable (drop nondet ops)
- perf counters: collect kernel selection trace, allocs, memcpy times, and flamegraphs
- iterations: min 300 measured iterations after warmup
- report: mean, 95p latency, tokens/sec, stddev, and CI

dez: add tokenization stability check: shuffle whitespace and compare token counts; different tokenizers give huge changes (esp. fp8 calibrations tied to token distribution).
rachel: for calibration experiments (fp8/int8): separate quality and perf. calibrate once per vocab/sample set and reuse the same calibration table across runs. record calibration dataset seed and size.
mike: yes. and for fairness: when comparing quant -> fp16, ensure kernel compiler flags identical (no extra autotune passes).
anya: perf probe command I used:```bash
./bench --model redwood-3-small --commit ab12cd --quant int8 --warmup 200 --tokens 1024 --power 250 --batch-dist ./hist.json --profile flame --kv-mode hot
```
anya: collect also: /proc/interrupts snapshot, nvidia-smi stats every 5s, and nvprof if possible.
perf-bot: regression alert acknowledged. created perf-ticket #4523 with attached traces.
mike: next steps: 1) eng-runtime will add a bench harness flag to enforce the protocol, 2) eng-ml will produce a canonical calibration bundle and seed, 3) eng-platform will add power-cap workflows to the nightly cluster. meet Weds 10am?
rachel: works for me. I'll attach the canary traces to the ticket and mark the regression severity as P2 for now.
de z: small nit: call the bench flag --protocol-version=1 so we can evolve it.
mike: agreed. thanks all. :thumbsup:
